knowledge.title: Big-O Notation and Complexity Classes
knowledge.content: Big-O notation describes the upper bound of an algorithm's growth rate. Common classes: O(1) constant, O(log n) logarithmic, O(n) linear, O(n log n) linearithmic, O(n²) quadratic, O(2ⁿ) exponential, O(n!) factorial. Big-O ignores constant factors and lower-order terms. Formal definition: f(n) = O(g(n)) iff ∃c,n₀ such that ∀n≥n₀: f(n) ≤ c·g(n).

knowledge.title: Array Data Structure
knowledge.content: An array stores elements in contiguous memory. Access: O(1) by index. Insert/Delete at end: O(1) amortized. Insert/Delete at position: O(n). Search unsorted: O(n). Search sorted (binary): O(log n). Arrays have fixed size in static languages, dynamic in Python/lists.

knowledge.title: Linked List Data Structure
knowledge.content: A linked list consists of nodes, each containing data and a reference to the next node. Singly linked: one direction. Doubly linked: forward and backward. Access: O(n). Insert/Delete at head: O(1). Insert/Delete at tail: O(1) with tail pointer. Memory overhead: one (singly) or two (doubly) pointers per node.

knowledge.title: Hash Map / Hash Table
knowledge.content: A hash map uses a hash function to map keys to bucket indices. Average case: O(1) for get/put/delete. Worst case (all collisions): O(n). Collision resolution: chaining (linked lists in buckets) or open addressing (probing). Load factor = n/buckets. Rehash when load factor exceeds threshold (typically 0.75).

knowledge.title: Binary Tree and BST
knowledge.content: A binary tree node has at most 2 children. Binary Search Tree (BST): left child < parent < right child. BST operations: search/insert/delete in O(h) where h is height. Balanced BST (AVL, Red-Black): h = O(log n). Unbalanced worst case: h = O(n) (degenerate to linked list). Traversals: inorder (LNR), preorder (NLR), postorder (LRN).

knowledge.title: Graph Data Structure
knowledge.content: A graph G = (V, E) consists of vertices V and edges E. Representations: adjacency matrix (O(1) edge lookup, O(V²) space) or adjacency list (O(degree) edge lookup, O(V+E) space). Directed vs undirected. Weighted vs unweighted. Cyclic vs acyclic (DAG). Traversal: BFS (queue, shortest path in unweighted), DFS (stack/recursion, topological sort).

knowledge.title: SOLID Principles
knowledge.content: S = Single Responsibility: one class, one reason to change. O = Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification. L = Liskov Substitution: subclasses must be substitutable for base classes. I = Interface Segregation: many specific interfaces over one general. D = Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions, not concretions.

knowledge.title: Concurrency: Threads and Synchronization
knowledge.content: Threads share memory space but have separate stacks. Synchronization primitives: mutex (mutual exclusion), semaphore (counter), condition variable (wait/notify), barrier (wait for N threads). Problems: race conditions, deadlock (circular wait), livelock, starvation. Solutions: lock ordering, timeouts, lock-free algorithms. GIL in CPython prevents true parallelism for CPU-bound threads.

knowledge.title: OSI Model and TCP/IP
knowledge.content: OSI 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application. TCP/IP 4 layers: Link, Internet, Transport, Application. Key protocols: HTTP/HTTPS (application), TCP/UDP (transport), IP (network), Ethernet (link). TCP: connection-oriented, reliable, ordered. UDP: connectionless, unreliable, low latency.

knowledge.title: Database Normalization
knowledge.content: Normalization reduces redundancy and anomalies. 1NF: atomic values, no repeating groups. 2NF: 1NF + no partial dependency on composite key. 3NF: 2NF + no transitive dependency. BCNF: every determinant is a candidate key. Denormalization trades redundancy for read performance. ACID properties: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

knowledge.title: CAP Theorem
knowledge.content: CAP theorem: a distributed system can guarantee at most 2 of 3 properties: Consistency (all nodes see same data at same time), Availability (every request gets a response), Partition tolerance (system continues despite network partitions). In practice: choose CP or AP since P is inevitable. Eventual consistency: system becomes consistent over time.

knowledge.title: Testing Pyramid
knowledge.content: Testing pyramid: many unit tests (bottom), fewer integration tests (middle), fewest E2E tests (top). Unit tests: test individual functions/classes in isolation (fast, cheap). Integration tests: test component interactions. E2E tests: test full system flow (slow, expensive). TDD: write tests before code (Red-Green-Refactor). Code coverage measures % of code executed by tests.
